narr: A weak cool front drifted south across the Red River Valley of Northeast Texas into Southern Arkansas during the daytime hours of July 2nd, as it was reinforced by a weak upper level trough shifting southeast through Eastern Oklahoma, Arkansas, and the Mississippi Valley. Low level moisture pooled out ahead of the front, with diurnal heating and weak forcing along the front contributing in an area of showers and thunderstorms across East Texas, Southern Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the morning and portions of the afternoon. Given the weakly sheared environment, these storms moved very slowly within the tropical air mass in place, with a cluster of storms producing very heavy rainfall affecting much of Ouachita Parish in North-Central Louisiana where widespread rainfall amounts of 1-3 inches fell. Due to the quick nature at which this heavy rainfall was observed, flash flooding was reported at various locations in West Monroe before diminishing during the afternoon.
ev: Several reports and pictures were posted to social media of flash flooding at the McMillian Road and North 7th Street intersection in West Monroe, as well as near Mill and Stella Streets.
lsr: SEVERAL REPORTS AND SOCIAL MEDIA PICTURES OF FLOODING IN WEST MONROE ON MCMILLIAN ROAD AND AROUND THE NORTH 7TH STREET INTERSECTION NEAR STELLA AND MILL STREETS.
